title: Thank You for the Present
focus: Present simple; like / love; this / it
paragraphs: Dear Aunt Marta,
Thank you for the lovely present! The blue backpack is beautiful, and it's very big. I can put all my books in it.
I use it every day. My friends like it, too. Valentina says it is very cool.
School is fine. I'm in Grade 6 now. My favourite class is Art, and my teacher is very nice. I have a new best friend, Zoe. She lives near my house, and we walk to school together.
How are you? Is it cold in Madrid? Here it is warm. Please come and visit us in December. You can sleep in my room!
Love,
Elena

title: Renata and Her Violin
paragraphs: Renata Morales is eleven years old, and she plays the violin. She is from Bogotá. She has a violin class every Tuesday and Thursday after school.
Renata practises for one hour every day. She doesn't like practising scales, but she loves playing songs. Her favourite songs are from Colombia and Spain.
Next month, Renata is playing in a concert with thirty children from different schools. She is nervous, but she is excited. Her parents and her grandmother are coming to the concert.
Renata says: 'Music is my best friend. When I'm sad, I play the violin and I feel better.' She can also play the piano a little, but the violin is her favourite instrument.

Drinks: water $1, lemonade $2, cola $2. Salad: small $3, big $5. Our garlic bread is $3.
Today's offer: any pizza and two drinks for $12 (Monday to Thursday). Kids' menu: small pizza with juice, only $6. We don't take credit cards, only cash.

title: Our Classroom Rules
paragraphs: Welcome to Class 6B! These are our classroom rules. We write them together every year.
We arrive on time. School starts at 7:30. We say 'Good morning' to our teacher and our classmates.
We listen when someone is speaking. We raise our hand to ask a question. We don't shout. We don't use phones in class, but we can use them at break.
We keep the classroom clean. We put rubbish in the bin. We help our friends when they have a problem. Our teacher, Mr Peña, says: 'Be kind, be honest and have fun!'

title: The Dog at the Bus Stop
paragraphs: Every morning, Camilo takes the bus to school. At the bus stop, there is a small brown dog. The dog is thin and has no collar.
Camilo has a sandwich in his bag. He gives half to the dog. The dog eats it quickly and wags his tail. 'You are hungry, my friend,' says Camilo.
Every day, the dog is at the bus stop and Camilo gives him some food. One day, the dog isn't there. Camilo is worried. He looks in the street and under the benches. Nothing.
In the afternoon, a girl is at the bus stop with the dog. 'This is Choco,' she says. 'He lives with my family now! Thanks for your food.' Camilo is very happy. Choco has a new red collar!

title: My Drawing Hobby
paragraphs: Hi! I'm Gabo and I love drawing. I draw every day after school. It is a quiet hobby, but I think it is very exciting!

I have a big notebook, ten pencils and a box of markers. I usually draw animals and robots. My dog, Luna, is my favourite model. She sits on the floor, but she doesn't stay still for more than two minutes.

I can't draw people very well, because faces are difficult. My art teacher says, 'Practise every day!' So I draw one face every Saturday. Look at my drawing: it's my mum. She is smiling, but her nose is too big!
I also have a small art club with three friends. We meet on Wednesdays at four o'clock. Do you draw, too? Send me your pictures, and I can put them on my blog!

title: A Surprise for Mum
paragraphs: Dad: Hi family! Mum's birthday is on Sunday. Let's make a plan.
Lucía: I can make the cake. Chocolate cake is her favourite!
Dad: Great. I can buy flowers on Saturday. Tomás, what can you do?
Tomás: I can make a card. And I can clean the living room.
Grandma: I can bring my famous rice. We can eat at one o'clock.
Dad: Perfect! Remember: it's a surprise. Don't tell Mum!

title: Greetings from Mexico City
focus: Present continuous; there is / there are
paragraphs: Hello Abuelo,
Greetings from Mexico City! I'm here with my parents for a few days. The city is enormous, and there are lots of people.
Today we are in Chapultepec Park. There is a big lake, a zoo and a castle. We are eating tacos on a bench. They are very spicy, but very good!
Tomorrow we're visiting the pyramids of Teotihuacán. My dad says they are very old. I'm taking lots of photos for you.
The weather is nice, and the people are friendly. I miss you! See you on Sunday.
Hugs,
Diego

title: Review: Café Luna
focus: Adjectives; there is / there are; present simple
paragraphs: Café Luna is a small café near my school. I go there with my friends on Fridays after class.
The coffee isn't expensive, and the hot chocolate is delicious. There are good sandwiches, too. My favourite is the cheese and tomato sandwich. It costs only $3.
The café is quiet and clean. There are comfortable chairs and there is free Wi-Fi. The music is nice, but sometimes it is loud.
The waiters are friendly. But there is a problem: the café is very small, and on Fridays it is full. We always want the table near the window, so we arrive early. I give it four stars out of five!
